task.name: Filtered PWM and ADC sweep
task.description: Sweeps PWM duty through a 10 kohm and 1 uF RC filter and prints raw ADC counts, not calibrated volts.
task.source:
# Written by BenchVista: pwm-adc-sweep 1.0.0, sha256 06f4048d7ac7560d2bb2fc0d092871bb08eb084553c562f806d3bd89780ed147
PINS = {"OUT": "J1.4", "IN": "J1.5"}
SETTINGS = {"samples": 8, "settle": 250}

# Filtered PWM and ADC sweep, a Spark Plug. CC0-1.0. Needs the Spark PWM/ADC task API.
# SAME 3.3 V board: OUT -> 10 kohm -> IN; IN -> 1 uF -> GND.
# Use a ceramic capacitor. Disconnect external circuits. Never connect 5 V.
# The RC filter averages PWM; without it ADC readings depend on pulse phase.
# 10..60% duty nominally means about 0.33..1.98 V on a 3.3 V supply.
# Prints raw scaled ADC counts, NOT calibrated volts or 16-bit accuracy.
def main(spark):
    settle = round(SETTINGS["settle"])
    samples = SETTINGS["samples"]
    print("duty_percent,adc_raw_mean")
    for percent in (10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10):
        spark.pwm(PINS["OUT"], 1000, round(percent * 65535 / 100))
        yield spark.sleep_ms(settle)
        total = 0
        for sample in range(samples):
            total += spark.adc_read_u16(PINS["IN"])
            yield spark.sleep_ms(5)
        print(percent, round(total / samples), sep=",")
    spark.pwm(PINS["OUT"], 1000, 0)
    yield spark.sleep_ms(100)

driverSources.name: the SH1106 example
driverSources.source:
"""SH1106 OLED, 128 x 64, on I2C: a Spark driver for BenchVista. CC0-1.0.

The controller holds 132 columns and its panel shows the middle 128, so every page is sent from
column 2. A one-bit frame in MONO_VLSB order, which is the controller's own page layout, sent
page by page by show(). The setup values are the datasheet's own after power-on.
"""
import framebuf

COMMANDS = 0x00
DATA = 0x40


class Driver:
    def __init__(self, bus, settings):
        self.bus = bus
        self.width = settings['width']
        self.height = settings['height']
        self.pages = self.height//8
        self.buffer = bytearray(self.pages*self.width)
        self.frame = framebuf.FrameBuffer(self.buffer, self.width, self.height, framebuf.MONO_VLSB)
        self.bus.writeto_mem(COMMANDS, bytes((
            0xae,           # display off
            0xd5, 0x80,     # clock
            0xa8, 0x3f,     # 64 lines
            0xd3, 0x00,     # no display offset
            0x40,           # start line 0
            0xad, 0x8b,     # internal DC-DC converter on
            0xa1,           # column 131 is segment 0
            0xc8,           # scan from COM[N-1]
            0xda, 0x12,     # COM pin layout
            0x81, 0x80,     # contrast
            0xd9, 0x22,     # pre-charge
            0xdb, 0x35,     # VCOM deselect level
            0xa4,           # show the frame
            0xa6,           # not inverted
        )))
        self.frame.fill(0)
        self.show()
        self.bus.writeto_mem(COMMANDS, bytes((0xaf,)))  # display on

    def show(self):
        view = memoryview(self.buffer)
        for page in range(self.pages):
            # The page, then column 2 as its low and high halves.
            self.bus.writeto_mem(COMMANDS, bytes((0xb0 | page, 0x02, 0x10)))
            self.bus.writeto_mem(DATA, view[page*self.width:(page+1)*self.width])
